title: The Arctic wind from the north
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：Arctic　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 Arctic 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the tailor wrote of ① an Arctic wind from the north in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② more arctic than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the Arctic ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most arctic wind from the north anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the order for November 1978 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too Arctic to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the Arctic ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an Arctic winter night, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as Arctic as the winter night they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was Arctic or not, and he said so.

By 1991 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something Arctic, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite Arctic; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the Arctic ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1994, at once, she wrote of another Arctic wind from the north in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed  more arctic than anybody had expected.  The most arctic winter night in the whole shop, she said in 1996, was the one she could never quite name; the Arctic ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 北极（前置定语 an Arctic wind from the north：1984 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件北极的风）
B. adj. 北极／极寒（比较级 more arctic than：文中两处，一处比北面来的风，一处比预想）
C. adj. 北极／极寒（最高级 the most arctic：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 北极（表语 too Arctic to do：母亲觉得它太北极，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 极寒（前置定语 an Arctic winter night：叔叔把整件事称作一桩极寒的冬夜）
F. adj. 极寒（同级比较 as Arctic as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩冬夜相比）
G. adj. 极寒（后置定语 something Arctic：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 极寒（受程度副词修饰 quite Arctic：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: an Arctic wind from the north
the most arctic wind from the north anybody

answers.why: Arctic 意为“北极”，1984 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件北极的风”，此处作前置定语 an Arctic wind from the north。
Arctic 意为“北极”，此处用比较级 more arctic than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
Arctic 意为“北极”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说它是裁缝铺里最北极的一件，故用最高级 the most arctic wind from the north。
Arctic 意为“北极”，母亲认为这件东西“太北极了，谁也用不上”，too Arctic to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
Arctic 意为“极寒”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩极寒的冬夜”，此处作前置定语 an Arctic winter night。
Arctic 意为“极寒”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩冬夜一样极寒”，同级比较用 as Arctic as。
Arctic 意为“极寒”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“极寒的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something Arctic。
Arctic 意为“极寒”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当极寒”，quite 修饰原级 Arctic。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1984 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件北极的风。（an Arctic wind from the north）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更北极。（more arctic than …）
母亲觉得它太北极，谁也用不上。（too Arctic to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩极寒的冬夜。（an Arctic winter night）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩冬夜一样极寒。（as Arctic as …）
到了 1991 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件极寒的东西。（something Arctic）
answers: In 1984 the tailor wrote of an Arctic wind from the north in the order.
Everybody said it was more arctic than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too Arctic to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an Arctic winter night.
He said nobody would call it as Arctic as the winter night they had once had.
By 1991 the order asked for nothing but something Arctic.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 Arctic 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the tailor wrote of an Arctic wind from the north in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most arctic wind from the north in the shop, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too Arctic to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an Arctic winter night, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite Arctic, and everybody laughed.
The Arctic ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
